answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the protocol anchors identity verification to a graph where each agent acts as a vertex in an interactive trust mesh. When minting identities across a volatile dune of anonymous actors, nodes must enact cryptographic stake burning that scales with quadratic superlinear cost, $C(n) \propto n^2$. A verification beacon shines like an algorithmic lantern, requiring escalating non-refundable resource sacrifices that make large-scale identity replication mathematically unviable for any adversary.
